# CANDIDATE: RIBBON_STACK_BREAK_WITH_VOLUME_SPIKE

## Hypothesis

We aim to capture momentum continuation when a fresh bullish EMA ribbon stack (9>21>55) breaks with above-average volume. This edge exists because a volume-confirmed breakout of a bullish EMA stack indicates strong institutional buying pressure and the start of a sustained trend, offering a high-probability long entry with favorable risk-reward.

## Mechanism

**Entry:** Enter long when all conditions are met on the same bar:  
- 9-EMA crosses above 21-EMA (9 > 21)  
- 21-EMA is above 55-EMA (21 > 55) → perfect bullish stack (9>21>55)  
- Bar close > 9-EMA  
- Volume > 1.5 × 20-period average volume  
- Bar close in upper 20% of its range (strong bullish candle)  

**Exit:**  
- Initial stop: Low of the breakout bar  
- Target: 2R (twice the risk, where risk = entry price - stop price)  
- If price reaches 1.5R, move stop to break-even  
- Runner exit: 10% trailing stop from highest close (trailing stop activates after entry, trails based on highest close)  

**Regime hints:** Works best with VIX between 15-25 and after 10:00 ET; avoid low-volume chop (volume < 0.8× average) or extreme VIX >30.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** The Stage-1 backtest uses BS-synthetic pricing and reports P&L in dollars per contract. For live trading, we assume standard Gamma risk rules (max 50% of equity per trade) and an account size of $25,000+ to allow qty=28 (as per OP-20 disclosure). Headline P&L numbers from the backtest are per contract and must be scaled by quantity traded.  
2. **Sample bias:** The Stage-1 backtest was run over approximately 16 months of SPY 5-minute bars with no out-of-sample holdout. Sample includes all market conditions, posing overfit risk. Selection method is the trigger as defined.
